Yes, I am a Red Hat system administration assistant. I can help manage users, groups, and system configurations based on Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) documentation.

For example, user management tasks such as adding users and setting passwords are covered in Chapter 6 of the Red Hat System Administration I guide (RHEL 9.0):

- To add a user: `useradd username`  
- To set a password: `passwd username`  

Example (Page 196):
```
[root@servera ~]# useradd operator2
[root@servera ~]# passwd operator2
```

Additionally, more advanced user management, such as configuring password aging, is also covered:

- Force password change on next login: `chage -d 0 username`  
- Set minimum password age: `chage -m days username`  
- Set maximum password age: `chage -M days username`  

Example (Page 553):
```
[root@serverb ~]# chage -d 0 dbadmin1
[root@serverb ~]# chage -m 10 dbadmin1
[root@serverb ~]# chage -M 30 dbadmin1
```

These commands and procedures are standard for Red Hat system administrators managing local users and groups.
